message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look list of the long‑weekend periods in Canada for 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a statutory holiday that either falls on a weekday or is observed on a Monday, giving you an extra day off.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if different) | Long‑Weekend Period |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Jan 1–3** (Fri Dec 30–Sun Jan 1) |
| Family Day (AB, BC, MB, ON, SK) | Monday Feb 20 | — | **Feb 18–20** (Sat Feb 18–Mon Feb 20) |
| Good Friday (all provinces) | Friday Mar 10 | — | **Mar 10–12** (Fri Mar 10–Sun Mar 12) |
| Victoria Day (all provinces) | Monday May 22 | — | **May 20–22** (Sat May 20–Mon May 22) |
| Canada Day | Thursday Jul 1 | — | **Jul 1–3** (Thu Jul 1–Sat Jul 3) |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | — | **Sep 2–4** (Sat Sep 2–Mon Sep 4) |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | — | **Oct 7–9** (Sat Oct 7–Mon Oct 9) |
| Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 | Observed Mon Nov 13 | **Nov 11–13** (Sat Nov 11–Mon Nov 13) |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | — | **Dec 23–25** (Sat Dec 23–Mon Dec 25) |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday Dec 26 | — | **Dec 24–26** (Sat Dec 24–Mon Dec 26) |

> **Note:** Some holidays (e.g., Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Remembrance Day, Christmas, Boxing Day) are observed on the same day they fall on. When a holiday falls on a weekend, the *observed* day is usually the following Monday, which still gives you a long weekend.

Feel free to use this table in your holiday‑planning app!
